# cg-slices-1470.txt   (WP-R of round 6; generator Paul/Python/gaudin_sl3/slice_engine.py `python -X utf8 slice_engine.py ref 14 7`; 2026-10-21)
# Highest-weight (HW) Clebsch-Gordan data of gl(3), V_Lambda (x) V_Lambda with Lambda = {14,7,0} (dim V = DIM): for EVERY irrep mu of the decomposition the PRV/Zhelobenko slice space M_mu, the exact matrix of the Gaudin vertex operator V on it, and its eigen-copies (the SoV copies).
# FORMAT: one record per line, TAB-separated fields, first field = tag, other fields nested braces = lists (Wolfram InputForm style). p/q = exact rationals. Reals marked "30 digits" are plain decimals (no exponent) with up to 30 significant digits, trailing zeros stripped, so exact values like 2.5 appear short (Mathematica: SetPrecision[ToExpression[s],30]; python: mpmath.mpf(s)); residuals are Python floats (e.g. 1.2e-15). Lines starting with # are comments.
# ORDER OF THE ONE-SITE GT BASIS (binding for every index below): the order of Paul/Python/gl3_reps.GL3Rep(Lambda).patterns = ascending lexicographic in (m1,m2,k) of the pattern {{k},{m1,m2},{l1,l2,l3}}; the HIGHEST-WEIGHT state is the LAST index (= DIM). All indices nu, idx are 1-BASED in this order. GTBASIS lists the patterns in exactly this order (same record format as W4).
#   The notebook/W4 order (ref/untwisted-exact-*.txt, Reverse@Sort of the patterns = descending lexicographic in (k,m1,m2), index 1 = highest weight) is DIFFERENT: map by pattern (python: nu_general.w4_to_mine). Matrices act on kets as columns, E e_col = sum_row M[row,col] e_row (plain rational non-unitary GT matrices of gl3_reps), E13 = [E12,E23], E31 = [E32,E21]. WEIGHTS1 = (E11,E22,E33) eigenvalues per index; GMET1 = invariant diagonal metric G (E_ij^T G = G E_ji, G[HW] = 1; equals W4 GMET1 up to the order).
# TWO SITES: Psi = sum Psi[nu,q] e_nu (x) e_q, site 1 = first factor (nu, slow), site 2 = second factor (q, fast); 1-based flat index idx = (nu-1)*DIM + q (nu,q 1-based, GL3Rep order). The SLICE of a vector Psi of weight mu is psi_top[nu] = Psi[nu, q_top] (site 2 = HW state q_top = index DIM), a vector in the weight space V_Lambda[mu-Lambda] (weight space = all nu whose GT weight equals mu-Lambda; W4 record `cg` = the same slice).
# THEOREM USED (Zhelobenko/PRV): Psi -> slice is an isomorphism from the HW vectors of weight mu onto M_mu = { v in V_Lambda[mu-Lambda] : E12^(l1-l2+1) v = 0, E23^(l2-l3+1) v = 0 }; dim M_mu = m = multiplicity of mu (Racah-Speiser, checked for every irrep). The full vector is recovered from the slice by a triangular recursion over the weights of site 2 (slice_engine.py, exact twin available).
# VERTEX OPERATOR: V = 1/2 Sum_{s,t in S3} sgn(s) sgn(t) e1_{s1 t1} e1_{s2 t2} e2_{s3 t3} (36 terms, e^k_ij = E_ij on site k, product in the written order), the notebook V (Minimal_complete_working-fast.wl vTriples). On a slice v in M_mu: V_red v = 1/2 Sum sgn sgn E_{s1 t1} E_{s2 t2} Phi_{s3 t3} v, Phi_cc = lambda_c, Phi_ab = -E_ab (a<b), Phi_ab = 0 (a>b) (no n_W-sized object needed; verified against the full 36-term V on the reconstructed vectors).
# RELATION TO W4/Laurent DATA (exact on all 45 branches of W4 files 110,210,220,310,320,410; see RESULTS-slice-engine.md): alpha_1(W4) = eigenvalue(V_red) + eta1/2, eta1 = |Lambda|^2 + cas2(Lambda) - cas2(mu)/2 = |Lambda|^2 - Omega with Omega = Sum_ij E1_ij E2_ji = (cas2(mu) - 2 cas2(Lambda))/2, |Lambda| = l1+l2+l3, cas2(mu) = Sum_i mu_i (mu_i + 4 - 2 i) (= W4 cas2); i.e. eigenvalue = alpha_1 - eta1/2 (alpha_1 = theta12 * a_1, a_1 = double-pole coefficient of S3 at theta_1). copy 1 = smaller eigenvalue = smaller alpha_1 (W4 convention).
# RECORDS: REP {l1,l2,l3} | DIM | GTBASIS | WEIGHTS1 | GMET1 | NSECTORS | NCOPIES | then per sector (descending lexicographic mu): SECTOR, WSPACE, PRVBASIS x m, VRED, CHARPOLY, then per copy COPY, HWRESID, GNORM2, then VEC x m (small reps) |
#   SECTOR mu m w nW dimVmu cas2mu eta1 : m = multiplicity = dim M_mu; w = dim V_Lambda[mu-Lambda] = length of a slice (NOT W4s third field); nW = dim of the weight-mu subspace of V (x) V (size of a full vector); dimVmu = dim of the irrep mu; cas2mu, eta1 as above |
#   PRVBASIS mu {{nu,val},...} : one line per basis vector of M_mu, k = 1..m in line order; EXACT rationals; nonzero entries of the slice on V_Lambda[mu-Lambda]; canonical basis = RREF nullspace with columns in ascending GT index, basis vector k = 1 at the k-th free column and 0 at the other free columns |
#   WSPACE mu {nu,...} : the 1-based GT indices (ascending) of the weight space V_Lambda[mu-Lambda]; the slice/PRVBASIS positions are aligned with this list |
#   VRED mu {{...},...} : exact m x m matrix of V_red in the PRVBASIS (list of ROWS; column j = V_red b_j in PRV coordinates, i.e. V_red b_j = Sum_i VRED[i][j] b_i) |
#   CHARPOLY mu {c0,c1,...,cm} : exact characteristic polynomial det(x 1 - V_red) = Sum_k c_k x^k (c_m = 1; ascending powers, exact rationals); its roots are the eigenvalues of the COPY records (= the V-spectrum, the pencil roots of the Q-system) |
#   COPY mu k eigenvalue {{nu,val},...} : the SoV copies = eigenvectors of V_red; k = 1..m by INCREASING eigenvalue (30 digits); the slice (30 digits) is scaled so that its FIRST NONZERO component (ascending nu) is exactly 1; components below 1e-40 relative to the largest (exact zeros of the algebraic eigenvector at 60 working digits) are dropped |
#   HWRESID mu k residual : max over i in {12,23,13} of ||(E_i (x) 1 + 1 (x) E_i) Psi|| / ||Psi|| for the full vector reconstructed (floating point, orthonormal GT basis, ||.|| = invariant norm) from COPY k |
#   GNORM2 mu k value : G-norm^2 (invariant norm, sum_{nu,q} g_nu g_q |Psi[nu,q]|^2, double precision, e-notation) of the FULL vector whose slice is COPY k (slice scaled with first nonzero component 1); multiply by the squared scale to compare with W4 gnorm2 |
#   (no VEC records in this file: full vectors have nW up to the table value; regenerate with slice_engine.hw_from_slice / the exact twin)
# SUMMARY (self-check of this file): 113 sectors, 344 copies; max HWRESID 2.64e-14; max eigen-residual |V_red c - ev c|/|c| 2.04e-57 (60 digits); min relative gap between consecutive eigenvalues of a sector 1.927e-02
